Why your laptop fan spins up on video calls

Video calls ask the processor to encode your camera and decode several streams at once, and that sustained load heats the chassis. The fan responds before the temperature becomes a problem.

A few small changes help. Close tabs that play audio in the background, lower the camera resolution in the call settings, and keep the vents clear by lifting the back of the laptop an inch.

If the fan is loud even when the machine is idle, a build up of dust is the usual cause. Compressed air through the vents once a year is normally enough.
